gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-inscripti: Big round lowercase bowls give Bloody its commanding, slightly bloody swagger. Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian reads like a wide-eyed sans, every e and a open, with a deep middle band that carries paragraphs easily.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-kayah-li: Bloody hits with big round lowercase bowls and a commanding, slightly bloody attitude. Noto Sans Kayah Li keeps text moving, brush ends lifting away before each curve closes and capitals barely taller than the lowercase.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-kharoshth: Big round lowercase bowls make Bloody feel commanding and a touch bloody, all swagger. Noto Sans Kharoshthi counters with curves that never close back on themselves, laying a thick, dark stripe of lowercase through each line.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Big, round, commanding: Bloody arrives with its lowercase bowls swinging. Noto Sans Khmer is the counterweight, with openings like chisel notches in wood and small letters standing proud, almost capital-sized.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Bloody brings big round lowercase bowls and a commanding, faintly bloody mood, loud enough to fill the whole line by itself. Noto Sans Khojki reads easily, its wide exits passing light through.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-kr: Rounded bowls, big in the lowercase, give Bloody a commanding, slightly bloody punch up top. And Noto Sans KR steadies it, keeping curve gaps generous and ascenders stubby beside a big x-height.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Noto Sans Lisu keeps tiny gaps between its ascender tops and the x-height line, and its s curves open wide. Noto Sans Lisu, if enlarged, would crowd Bloody's big bowls.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-malayalam: Big round lowercase bowls carry Bloody's commanding, slightly bloody look, while Noto Sans Malayalam fills its lines with a dominant middle zone. Give Bloody plenty of size and let the body stay modest.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-mandaic: Commanding from the first letter, Bloody rounds out its lowercase into big bowls. Noto Sans Mandaic runs on curvy, unclamped letters, with lowercase rising close to capitals, so paragraphs feel loose and easy going.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-mayan-num: Bloody's big round lowercase bowls hit hard and look commanding. Noto Sans Mayan Numerals offers the sharpest foil here: tall-bodied small letters and a visibly gaping c at any size.
